newsitem.title: FRANCE: Lyonnaise to sign Budapest water deal on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: Lyonnaise to sign Budapest water deal on Tuesday.

text.p: Lyonnaise des Eaux, which agreed on Friday to merge with Cie de Suez, will on Tuesday sign a water treatment contract for the Hungarian capital of Budapest, a newspaper said on Sunday.

Lyonnaise chairman Jerome Monod told Le Journal Du Dimanche in an interview that the group was also finalising a wide-ranging water and electricity deal for Casablanca in Morocco. He also confirmed telecoms talks with Bouygues.

"We recently won a very big contract for Manila (Phillipines) for seven million inhabitants. I have to sign on Tuesday a contract for Budapest (two million inhabitants). Meanwhile we are finalising a very important agreement for the purification and distribution of water as well as electricity in Casablanca," Monod said.
He added that there were still some one billion people who live in towns that do not yet have water distribution and purification systems.
"The Lyonnaise (des Eaux) was created in 1880 by Credit Lyonnais. Since 1989, our main aim is international. In water, our goal is to double our foreign revenues in the next five years," he said.
Monod said that Lyonnaise wanted to become more deeply involved in the French market for electricity once the monopoly of Electricite de France is scaled down due to European liberalisation.

Monod confirmed that Lyonnaise was in talks with Bouygues on telecommunications, but he indicated the discussions were not as all-encompasing as a rumoured tie-up between Lyonnaise Communication and Bouygues Telecom, itself allied to Italy's STET and Germany's VEBA.
"Our discussions with Bouygues are in particular about the future of telephony using the cable," Monod said.
Lyonnaise des Eaux is one of France's biggest operators of television cable networks after France Telecom.
Bouygues, a construction group which also controls France's biggest commercial television broadcaster TF1, plans to become a major telecom operator in France, rivalling France Telecom and Cegetel.
Cegetel, a venture of Generale des Eaux, BT Plc and Germany's Mannesmann AG, recently signed an important deal with railroad operator SNCF to use the latter's nationwide fibre optic network.
Bouygues had also been bidding for the SNCF deal to use the network as an alternative infrastructure to lines leased from France Telecom.

"The cable networks of Lyonnaise des Eaux are nearly at break-even and in Paris they make a profit. The cable, thanks to digitalisation will become an exceptional resource because it is capable of transporting voice, data and images. It will play an important role in the future of telecommunications," Monod said.
"That is why we are looking for French or foreign partners," Monod told le Journal du Dimanche.
